subject: HSM migration validation & SOC2 evidence exchange
messages:
From: Sam Greene <sam.greene@asterislabs.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: security@asterislabs.com
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HSM migration validation & evidence needed for SOC2 audit

Hi Diego,

Quick note from the Asteris security team — our SOC2 auditor has requested a compact evidence bundle for the upcoming migration of your tenant keys from the legacy HSM cluster (hsm-old-1) into your new HSM pool (hsm-2027-cluster). Specifically they want:

- Migration runbook showing operator steps and separation of duties
- Signed ceremony minutes (key-export/wrap events) or an attestation if you used split-ceremony tooling
- Sample shift logs showing operator IDs and timestamped actions for at least two rotations during July
- Transport proofs for wrapped KEKs (filenames, checksums) and SFTP delivery plan

Would it be possible to provide a short migration validation packet and a timeline for when we can review? Our auditor prefers one consolidated package rather than piecemeal uploads.

Thanks — we aim to close this checklist by Aug 20.

Sam Greene
Security Manager, Asteris Labs
sam.greene@asterislabs.com

[attachment: audit-scope-asteris-2027.pdf]
From: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Greene <sam.greene@asterislabs.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HSM migration validation & evidence needed for SOC2 audit

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. High-level plan:

1) Provide a single ZIP-style evidence packet containing the runbook, ceremony minutes, operator shift logs (redacted PII where appropriate), and transport manifest.
2) Deliverables will be uploaded to the secure Drive link and we will provision SFTP access to a dropbox for the auditor with a one-time key.
3) Timeline: draft packet by EOD Aug 16; final signed artifacts (with engineering + security sign-off) by Aug 19.

Marissa I’m assigning the runbook and minutes compilation to you (see itemized checklist in attached).
Kimberly can you pull the operator shift logs and the KEK wrap manifests from the HSM telemetry? We’ll need checksums and the signing operator IDs.

Sam — can you confirm the preferred checksum algorithm (sha256 vs sha512) and whether the auditor wants original filenames preserved?

Diego Fernandez
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | Redwood Inference
[attachment: diego-assignment-checklist.txt]
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HSM migration validation & evidence needed for SOC2 audit

Thanks — quick status update and notes.

- Runbook: compiled into hsm-migration-plan-v1.pdf (covers pre-checks, operator separation, quorum rules, network cutover steps, rollback plan).
- Ceremony minutes: we have a signed minutes PDF but one of the signatures is pending (cloudops lead was traveling). I included a notarized attestation header while we wait; final signed minutes to follow by Aug 19.
- Operator shift logs: extracted two sample shifts (2027-07-05 and 2027-07-28). I redacted personal emails and included operator IDs and shift tokens.
- KEK manifests: kimberly — can you confirm that the wrapped KEK files are named using the new cluster prefix (hsm-2027-) and include checksums?

Proposed upload schedule: draft packet (no signatures) to Drive by 16:30 PDT today; SFTP access and final ZIP after signatures no later than Aug 19.

Attachments: keks-checklist.xlsx (working), sftp-instructions.txt (dropbox details).

Marissa Cole
Security Programs | Redwood Inference

Diego / team — appreciate the rapid turnaround. Auditor prefers sha256 checksums and preserving original filenames where possible. The single-package preference stands — they like a consistent manifest at the top level naming each file and its checksum.

One small ask: please include a short notes.txt at the root of the package that lists any redactions and the rationale (PII redaction, operator privacy). That speeds reviewer triage.

If you can hit the draft today we’ll start preliminary review and flag any missing items early.

Sam
